captions.instagram:
How does a camera actually see?

A dark box, a hole, and an upside-down world. Take a real camera apart in 3D and learn what aperture, shutter speed and ISO really do.

→ Every camera is just a dark box with a hole in it.
→ Bigger hole: a brighter picture, but a blurrier one.
→ A lens bends every ray back to one point. Bright and sharp.
→ Inside a real camera: lens, iris, shutter, sensor.
→ Aperture: wide melts the background. Narrow keeps it all sharp.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/cameraclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does a camera actually see? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
A dark box, a hole, and an upside-down world. Take a real camera apart in 3D and learn what aperture, shutter speed and ISO really do.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/cameraclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/glassboxhow/cameraclear

In this video:
• Every camera is a dark box with a hole. Light travels in straight lines.
• A lens fixes the pinhole's trade-off. A bigger hole gives a brighter picture but a blurrier one.
• Aperture is how wide the door opens. Iris blades set the size of the opening.
• Shutter speed is how long the door stays open. Two curtains slide across the sensor.
• ISO turns up the volume, and the noise. The sensor counts photons in millions of tiny wells.
• Exposure is the three working together. Aperture, shutter speed and ISO all trade against each other.
